title: Bounded separation of finite-rank Tate root modules
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] complete for a nontrivial real-valued multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute value, with $\operatorname{char}(k)=p>0$. Let $n\ge1$, $T=k\langle X_1,\ldots,X_nangle$ be the restricted-series ring [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation] with Gauss absolute value $G(\sum_
u a_
u X^
u)=\sup_
u|a_
u|$ (multiplicative and definite, so $T$ is an integral domain), and put $F=\operatorname{Frac}(T)$. In an algebraic closure $\overline F$, put $T^{1/p}=\{z\in\overline F:z^p\in T\}$ with norm $N(z)=G(z^p)^{1/p}$. Let $M\subseteq T^{1/p}$ be a $T$-submodule of finite rank, meaning that its $F$-linear span inside $F^{1/p}=\{z\in\overline F:z^p\in F\}$ has finite dimension. For every nonzero $x\in M$, there exist a $T$-linear map $\lambda:M	o T$ and a real $B>0$ with $\lambda(x)
e0$ and $$G(\lambda(y))\le B N(y)\qquad(y\in M).$$ No finite-degree hypothesis on $k^{1/p}/k$ is imposed.

The field $k_1$ is complete: if $(c_j)$ is Cauchy then $(c_j^p)$ is Cauchy in $k$, and the unique $p$th root of its limit is a limit of $(c_j)$, since $|c_i-c_j|_1^p=|c_i^p-c_j^p|$. The characteristic-$p$ identity for series is $(\sum c_

u)^p=\sum c_

u}$: for each coefficient it is the finite multinomial identity, whose mixed coefficients vanish modulo $p$. Thus $T	o A$, $X_i\mapsto Y_i^p$, identifies $A$ with $T^{1/p}$: take the unique coefficient roots of any $\sum a_
u X^
u\in T$ and then its unique root in $\overline F$. Restrictedness in both directions is exactly $|a_
u|=|a_
u^{1/p}|_1^p$. This is a ring identification over $T$, and $N(\sum c_

u)=\sup_

u^pX^
u)$. The Gauss norm is finite and definite by [lem-trf-restricted-series-gauss-completion].

source.place: 5.3.1/2 proof, printed pp.212-213: root-series identification, with the coefficient calculation written out.

proof.text: Choose $m_1,\ldots,m_r\in M$ which form an $F$-basis of its finite-dimensional $F$-span. Their series coefficients constitute an at most countable set $D\subset k_1$, since $r$ and $n$ are finite. Let $B_0=k[D]\subset k_1$. Every $b\in B_0$ satisfies $b^p\in k$; if $b\ne0$, then $b^{-1}=b^{p-1}/b^p\in B_0$. Hence $B_0$ is a field. It is spanned over $k$ by the countable set of finite monomials in $D$. Let $k^{\prime}$ be its metric closure in $k_1$. This closure is a field: addition and multiplication pass to limits, and if $b_j\to a\ne0$, eventually $|b_j|_1=|a|_1$, so $|b_j^{-1}-a^{-1}|_1=|b_j-a|_1/|a|_1^2\to0$. It is complete as a closed subset of the complete $k_1$, contains $k$ and $D$, and has the countable monomials as a set with dense $k$-linear span. Its absolute value is nontrivial on $k$. Set $S=k^{\prime}\langle Y_1,\ldots,Y_n\rangle\subset A$; all $m_i$ belong to $S$, and $T\subset S$ via $X_i=Y_i^p$.

source.place: 5.3.1/2 proof, printed p.213: choose a maximal independent family and its smallest complete coefficient field; countable-type assertion expanded.

proof.text: For every $m\in M$, its basis expression $m=\sum_i f_i m_i$ with $f_i\in F=\operatorname{Frac}(T)$ puts $m$ in $\operatorname{Frac}(S)$, since $T\subset S$ and $m_i\in S$. Also $m^p\in T\subset S$, so $m$ satisfies the monic polynomial $Z^p-m^p\in S[Z]$. Apply [lem-trf-tate-integrally-closed] with the complete field $K=k^{\prime}$ and $d=n$: this proves $m\in S$. Thus $M\subset S$, including elements outside the $T$-span of the chosen basis. The Gauss norm of $S$ is its inherited norm from $A$, so it is precisely $N$ on $M$.

source.place: 5.3.1/2 proof, printed p.213, last paragraph: rational-span containment and monic integrality; BGR 5.2.6/2 normality input replaced by its existing DAG node.

proof.text:
Partition exponents into residue classes modulo $p$. For $s=\sum_
u c_
u Y^
u\in S$ and $\alpha\in\{0,\ldots,p-1\}^n$, put $s_\alpha(X)=\sum_\mu c_{p\mu+\alpha}X^\mu\in k^{\prime}\langle Xangle$. These series are restricted because their coefficients are subfamilies of the coefficients of $s$. Comparing coefficients gives $s=\sum_\alpha Y^\alpha s_\alpha(X)$, uniquely, and $N(s)=\max_\alpha G_{k^{\prime}}(s_\alpha)$; here $G_{k^{\prime}}$ is the coefficient supremum over $k^{\prime}$. For $t\in T$, the finite Cauchy convolution gives $(ts)_\alpha=t s_\alpha$, so every projection $s\mapsto s_\alpha$ is $T$-linear and decreases the norm. Since $x
e0$, choose a nonzero coefficient $c$ of some $x_\alpha$. Apply [lem-trf-countable-type-bounded-dual] to the $k$-normed space $k^{\prime}$ from step 2 to get a $k$-linear $h:k^{\prime}	o k$ and $C>0$ with $h(c)
e0$ and $|h(a)|\le C|a|_1$ for all $a\in k^{\prime}$.

source.place: 5.3.1/2 proof, printed p.213: countable-type bounded dual and norm-direct residue-class decomposition; Proposition 2.7.1/2.

proof.text:
Define $H:k^{\prime}\langle Xangle	o T$ by $H(\sum_\mu a_\mu X^\mu)=\sum_\mu h(a_\mu)X^\mu$. It lands in restricted series and satisfies $G(H(f))\le C G_{k^{\prime}}(f)$, since $|h(a_\mu)|\le C|a_\mu|_1$. It is additive, and for $t=\sum_ eta b_ eta X^ eta\in T$ the coefficient at $
u$ of $H(tf)$ is $h(\sum_{ eta+\mu=
u}b_ eta a_\mu)=\sum_{ eta+\mu=
u}b_ eta h(a_\mu)$, exactly the coefficient of $tH(f)$. All sums here are finite, so only $k$-linearity is used; $h$ need not be multiplicative. Hence $\lambda(y)=H(y_\alpha)$ is a $T$-linear map $M	o T$. Its value on $x$ has the selected coefficient $h(c)
e0$, and $G(\lambda(y))\le C G_{k^{\prime}}(y_\alpha)\le C N(y)$ for every $y\in M$. Take $B=C$. If $M=0$ the assertion has no nonzero $x$ and is vacuous. No step bounds $[k_1:k]$.

from.place: Historical analytic input supporting the normalization chain from lem-trf-local-term-locality, through Temkin Theorem 3.5.5 Step 2: Distinguished presentations of reduced affinoids over an algebraically closed field. This is below the node level, not a replacement of the current contracting-correspondence unit proof. The displayed inequalities spell out the weakly cartesian topology for a finite basis. The item statement is BGR 5.3.1/2 b-separability written out; it is not weakened and assumes neither finite generation nor finite [k^{1/p}:k]. Step 1: k_1=k^{1/p} is complete, and Frobenius gives A=k_1<Y> ≅ T^{1/p} with N = coefficient supremum (checked). Step 2: the coefficients D are countable, k[D] is a field since b^p is in k, and its closure k' is a complete field (the inverse estimate is correct) of countable type. Step 3: m = sum of f_i m_i lies in Frac(S) and is a root of Z^p-m^p in S[Z]; integral closedness with K=k' gives M in S, including elements outside the T-span of the basis. Step 4: the residue decomposition is unique and preserves norms; (ts)_alpha = t s_alpha checked; the new node applies because |a|_1=|a| on k. Step 5: coefficientwise H is T-linear through finite sums and k-linearity, gives G(lambda y) <= C N(y), and lambda(x) has the coefficient h(c), which is nonzero. New node: true (t-orthogonal sequence starting at v over complete nontrivial k; completion and restriction for incomplete V). Small cases checked: V=k, finite-dimensional V, dense incomplete span. It is self-contained, statement-only, with all three kinds of search and correct blueprint fields, and is generic rather than a restatement of the item.
